headline: Single-cell and regulatory-genomics claims are tested against replicate, compressibility and genotype-effect nulls
label: Evaluation Choice Robustness Audits
summary: Four preprints test whether single-cell and sequence-model claims survive appropriate references, with several finding that the headline effect does not hold.
synthesis: The common thread is checking whether a computational claim survives an appropriate reference. In drug-tolerant PC9 cells, replicate libraries set the noise floor for cell-state contrasts, assessed with a library-level permutation test. A sequence model conditioned on single-cell snapshots predicts interferon-beta response in monocytes (Spearman 0.616, n=119 genes) but not stimulus-dependent genetic effects. The Computable Genomes framework tests sequence compressibility against reporter-assay variant effects and finds no support. ImmunoTwin is a different kind of study: it maps regulators from Perturb-seq screens and reports a replicated coupling of T-cell exhaustion markers with macrophage M1 activation in patients under checkpoint blockade. The new contribution is explicit negative or bounded results tied to a specific null or replication standard.
